rubrics.justification: Describes a blastocyst with strong A-grade ICM, looser B-grade TE, large blastocoel, and thinning zona in a way that is broadly consistent with a 3AB image; minor uncertainty around calling it full/early-expanded versus reported stage and some image-specific details may be inferred from a single still.

Integrates age, ovarian response, AMH/FSH, semen parameters, BMI, stress, prior cycle history, and endometrial thickness well, and appropriately relates these factors to embryo prognosis and transfer expectations.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent overall, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and patient factors; only minor issues include some overinterpretation of the DOR label inconsistency and modest uncertainty in the exact implantation range.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with common IVF practice: SET at age 32, no bed rest, optimize luteal support, cautious view of 7 mm lining, and selective rather than routine PGT-A. Minor deviation is the somewhat strong emphasis on lining thickness and stage terminology discussion.

Provides clear, practical next steps for the current transfer and contingency planning for future cycles, including SET, luteal support, OHSS monitoring, endometrial reassessment, cavity evaluation, and when to consider PGT-A or male-factor workup.
